root_cause: Supabase production migration lineage advanced outside repository source control. Six live migrations were initially missing locally; while that recovery was being merged, production also gained 20261007190600_security_definer_browser_execute_closure_v1. This proved that a one-time history capture can become stale during terminal delivery. The parity regression also used fileURLToPath from node:path instead of node:url, so post-merge learning replay failed even though the migration recovery itself was valid.
prevention: Mirror every already-applied production migration version into supabase/migrations with its real SQL rather than an empty compatibility stub.
Treat migration-history parity as a terminal readback condition: compare production history to the exact current-main migration directory again after protected merge, not only at candidate creation.
Refresh supabase/migration-history.lock.json from production migration history whenever remote lineage is reconciled.
Run tests/brain-supabase-remote-migration-history-parity-v1.test.mjs so every captured remote version must remain replayable from repository files.
Use fileURLToPath from node:url for ESM URL-to-path conversion so canonical learning replay is executable on Node 24.
Keep historical SECURITY DEFINER mirrors least-privilege for fresh replay even when the later live state was hardened by a subsequent migration.
Never repair migration drift by deleting, renumbering or rewriting production migration-history rows.
